claim_tested: Which IFT-B subunits IFT56 contacts, and how large the interface is
key_finding: IFT56 contacts only IFT46 (14 res), IFT70 (10), IFT52 (7) at <5 A; smallest normalised footprint of 13 subunits; betweenness 0.000; no lateral train contacts
context: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii cilia, in situ cryo-ET 9.9 A with AlphaFold2 models docked (PDB 8BD7)
confidence_and_limits: High for partner identity (reproduced in both repeats); moderate for residue-level detail because side chains are not resolved at 9.9 A

key_finding: Wild-type Ttc26 binds directly to the Ift46 subunit of IFT complex B
confidence_and_limits: High; independent of the structure and of the organism used for it

claim_tested: Do IFT56 and IFT46 form a module
key_finding: ARL13B interacts with the IFT46-IFT56 dimer of the IFT-B complex
confidence_and_limits: High for the IFT46-IFT56 dimer; the ARL13B link is a separate claim

claim_tested: Which partners co-purify with the DYF-13 ortholog
key_finding: PIFTC3 in a ~660 kDa complex with IFT-B components plus DYF-1 (IFT70), DYF-3, DYF-11, IFTA-2; also co-IP with IFT122 (IFT-A)
context: Trypanosoma brucei, affinity purification and mass spectrometry
confidence_and_limits: Moderate-high; the IFT122 contact is not reproduced in 8BD7 and may be indirect

claim_tested: Is TTC26/IFT56 a core or peripheral IFT-B subunit
key_finding: Assigns TTC26/IFT56 to the salt-resistant IFT-B core subcomplex by visible immunoprecipitation
confidence_and_limits: Moderate; biochemical salt-resistance and small structural footprint are compatible, so this qualifies rather than refutes

claim_tested: Is IFT56 needed to build or run the IFT train
key_finding: IFT particle assembly and speed are normal in dyf13 mutant flagella, unlike other IFT-B mutants; motility proteins specifically depleted
confidence_and_limits: High; directly matches the structural prediction that IFT56 is not a scaffold

claim_tested: Does IFT56 affect IFT-B composition in cilia
key_finding: Core IFT-B proteins IFT88, IFT81, IFT27 fail to accumulate in Ift56hop cilia; IFT-A unaffected
confidence_and_limits: High for the phenotype; the mechanism is not explained by the three small interfaces in 8BD7

claim_tested: Is DYF-13 an IFT protein in C. elegans
key_finding: dyf-13(mn396) ciliary structural defect maps to C27H5.7a; the protein undergoes IFT and its transport is disrupted by ift and bbs mutations
confidence_and_limits: High; the only direct C. elegans evidence, and it is not represented by any experimental-code GO annotation

claim_tested: Where does the IFT56 ortholog localise
key_finding: Ttc26 localised to the transition zone of photoreceptor cilia and of mIMCD3 cilia
confidence_and_limits: Moderate; transition zone differs from the ciliary base and basal body terms currently annotated IBA

claim_tested: Can convex/concave solenoid geometry place DYF-13 as scaffold or adaptor
key_finding: No. Arc radius 34.5 A; mapped contacts split 6 concave / 9 convex vs background 218/305, Fisher OR 1.07, p = 1.0
confidence_and_limits: High as a negative result; refutes this component of the seed hypothesis

claim_tested: Is the contact transfer to C. elegans independently supported
key_finding: DYF-6, OSM-6 and DYF-1 exist at 36-48% identity, but their IFT56-binding residues are no better conserved than background (Fisher p = 0.70-1.0)
context: Chlamydomonas vs C. elegans pairwise alignments
confidence_and_limits: High; means the transfer is orthology-based, not interface-validated

claim_tested: Does IFT-B account for the conserved surface of DYF-13
key_finding: No. All 4 conserved exposed patches (45-62, 166-373, 347-357, 378-414) lie outside the mapped contacts; the C-half 325-574 is conserved (0.452) and folded (pLDDT 91.9) yet contacts nothing
confidence_and_limits: Moderate-high; limited by 9.9 A resolution and by IFT-B2/cargo absent from the modelled repeat
